reproduction_target: Molecular substratification of metastatic prostate cancer along the DNA damage repair (DDR) axis and development of CHIMERA-DDR, a two-tier nested Random Forest probabilistic classifier over 51 genomic/transcriptomic features that infers 7 DDR subgroups. Computational target: WES/WGS alignment (BWA-MEM v0.7.17.1, GRCh38) and GATK Best-Practices preprocessing (Picard MarkDuplicates v2.24.1, BQSR v4.1.9.0); germline calling (GATK HaplotypeCaller with gnomAD v3.1.1 / 1000 Genomes / ESP6500 filtering) and somatic calling (MuTect2 + Strelka v2 union, BEDTools target filtration); TMB estimation (pyTMB v1.4.0); MSI scoring (MSIsensor-pro v1.2.0, cutoff 3.5); pathogenicity curation of 46 DDR genes (ANNOVAR, Mutalyzer 2.0, ACMG, cross-check against cBioPortal/ExAC/Kaviar/ClinGen/ClinVar/ClinVitae/CIViC/OncoKB/UniProt); allele-specific copy number, purity and ploidy (Sequenza v2.0.0) with homebrew gene-level annotation (pyTHiA-CNA, GENCODE v45); LOH / TAI / LST HRD-Scar scoring (Abkevich rules, Sztupinszky HRD-Scar tool); mutational signature extraction (SigProfilerExtractor v1.1.23, COSMIC v3.4, NMF); subgroup consensus copy number from pooled BAMs downsampled to 300x with Picard and CNVkit v0.9.12; RNA-seq alignment (STAR v2.7.3a, hg38) and quantification (GenomicAlignments), differential expression (edgeR + limma, filterByExpr, BH FDR), GSVA CCP/ARa/NEa signature scores; immune deconvolution (CIBERSORT v1.04, LM22, absolute mode, 100 permutations); clonal reconstruction (PhyloWGS v1.0-rc2, 4 MCMC chains) and visualisation (Clonevol v0.1); TMB cut-point selection by binary logistic regression with 3-fold cross-validation (18.61 mut/Mb); percent-genome-alteration estimation by the homebrew PGA_Estimator; CHIMERA-DDR nested Random Forest training, overfit assessment and semi-independent validation on a 52-sample multi-site WGS test cohort. Tissue acquisition (UW rapid autopsy), library preparation and WES/WGS/RNA sequencing, plus clinical-grade sequencing of the 130-patient clinical validation cohort, are W (out of computational-reproduction scope).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v2 full-text HTML (WebFetch of both the .source.xml and the .full URL returned HTTP 403; a direct curl of https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.10.08.680958v2.full with a browser user-agent returned HTTP 200 and contains the complete METHODS, Data Availability and Code Availability sections). No README prose could be read for any of the three stated repositories because all three GitHub URLs return HTTP 404 (Niel20/CHIMERA, Niel20/PGA_Estimator, Niel20/CHIMERA_DDR_Validation_Cohort_52_WGS) - the repositories are private, deleted or never created. The Code Availability statement itself gates access: 'all rights are reserved to Copyright 2025 Medical College of Wisconsin. For academic usage codes would be made available by request to corresponding author'. Version scoring rule applied here: a prose pin counts (version=1) only when the primary tool of the step carries at least major.minor - BWA-MEM v0.7.17.1, Picard v2.24.1, GATK BQSR v4.1.9.0, pyTMB v1.4.0, MSIsensor-pro v1.2.0, SigProfilerExtractor v1.1.23, Sequenza v2.0.0, CNVkit v0.9.12, STAR v2.7.3a, CIBERSORT v1.04, PhyloWGS v1.0-rc2 and Clonevol v0.1 qualify; MuTect2, 'Strelka v2', GATK HaplotypeCaller, BEDTools, ANNOVAR, edgeR, limma, GSVA, GenomicAlignments, the HRD-Scar tool, R and the Random Forest implementation behind CHIMERA-DDR do not. No lockfile, container image or digest, conda specification or release tag is claimed anywhere in the paper. Data axis: steps that consume raw reads or BAMs score 0 because no raw-sequence accession (SRA/dbGaP/EGA) is stated anywhere - the Data Availability statement points only to processed-level cBioPortal datahub directories and to three GEO series for UW-TAN RNA-seq; steps that consume processed variant/expression/copy-number level data score 1.

steps.label: Wet-lab: University of Washington rapid autopsy tissue acquisition (UW-TAN) and SU2C Dream Team specimen collection, nucleic acid extraction, WES / WGS / poly(A) RNA library preparation and sequencing of the 672-sample discovery cohort and the 52-sample multi-site WGS test cohort; plus clinical-grade genomic sequencing of the 130-patient clinical validation cohort at four academic medical centres. No wet-lab protocol, platform, capture kit or read length is described in Methods.

Alignment of WES and WGS reads to GRCh38/hg38 using Burrows-Wheeler Aligner-MEM v0.7.17.1 - exact tool pin, no command line, no reference build accession/checksum, and no raw-read accession for either cohort

GATK Best Practices preprocessing: alignment quality assessment, read sorting and duplicate marking with Picard MarkDuplicates v2.24.1, Base Quality Score Recalibration with GATK v4.1.9.0 - known-sites resources for BQSR are not named

Germline variant calling with GATK HaplotypeCaller followed by population-database filtering against gnomAD v3.1.1, 1000 Genomes and ESP6500 to exclude common variants at allele frequency >0.1% - allele-frequency threshold is exact and gnomAD is pinned, but no HaplotypeCaller/GATK version is given for this step and the 1000 Genomes and ESP6500 releases are unpinned

Somatic variant calling with MuTect2 and Strelka v2 in tumor-normal paired mode requiring minimum coverage of 12 high-quality reads (Q>=40) with at least 6 supporting alternate alleles, union of the two filtered call sets, then BEDTools filtration to target capture regions - thresholds are exact but MuTect2, BEDTools and the capture BED are unversioned/unidentified and 'Strelka v2' is a major version only

Tumor mutation burden estimation with pyTMB v1.4.0 from the union variant set, incorporating effective genome size and cellularity, after manual curation of all variants - exact tool pin, but the effective genome size value, the cellularity source and the pyTMB filter flags are not stated, and the manual curation step is unscripted and irreproducible

Microsatellite instability scoring with MSIsensor-pro v1.2.0 on paired tumor-normal WES and WGS, MSI-High defined at score >=3.5 and MSS below 3.5 - exact tool pin and exact threshold, but the microsatellite site list / baseline file is not identified

Pathogenicity classification of somatic and germline variants in 46 curated DNA-repair and tumor-suppressor genes: annotation with ANNOVAR, validation with Mutalyzer 2.0, ACMG rules for germline, five stated somatic pathogenicity criteria, and cross-validation against cBioPortal, ExAC, Kaviar, ClinGen, ClinVar, ClinVitae, CIViC, OncoKB and UniProt - the gene list is enumerated in prose but no ANNOVAR version, no annotation database builds, no database access dates, and the curation itself is manual with no released decision table

Allele-specific copy number, tumor cellularity, purity and ploidy inference with Sequenza v2.0.0 from paired tumor/normal depth of coverage and B-allele frequency - exact tool pin, no gc-wiggle window, no binning or segmentation parameters, and BAM inputs are not accessible

Gene-level copy number aberration annotation with the homebrew tools 'pyTHiA-CNA' and a 'homebrew annotator tool referencing GENCODE v45 annotation', and bi-allelic inactivation calling (pathogenic mutation plus copy loss at log2 ratio < -0.5 with LOH-consistent B-allele frequency, or complex structural aberration) - GENCODE is pinned and the bi-allelic thresholds are exact, but pyTHiA-CNA is described only in Supplementary Document 5 and is not published in any resolvable repository

LOH, telomeric allelic imbalance and large-scale state transition scoring and HRD-Scar summation using the HRD-Scar tool of Sztupinszky et al. with Abkevich LOH rules: events >15 Mb with non-zero copy number and inferred minor allele count 0, chromosomes with such events over >=75% of their length excluded from numerator and denominator - rules are exact but the HRD-Scar tool carries no version and no repository reference

COSMIC mutational signature extraction with SigProfilerExtractor v1.1.23 against the COSMIC v3.4 reference set: NMF with 100 replicates, resampling enabled, 10,000-1,000,000 iterations, convergence tolerance 1e-15, GRCh38 reference and opportunity genomes, default trinucleotide context; HRRd (signature 3), MMRd (6, 14, 15, 20, 21, 26, 44) and POLE (9, 10a-d, 14, 20) signatures scored - the most fully specified step in the paper, but no random seed is reported for the NMF replicates

Subgroup-specific consensus copy number: discovery-cohort BAMs pooled per DDR molecular subgroup, downsampled to 300x depth with Picard tools, then CNVkit v0.9.12 applied to the pooled downsampled BAMs - CNVkit is pinned and the 300x target is exact, but no Picard DownsampleSam version or seed, no CNVkit reference/target/antitarget construction, and pooled BAMs are not accessible

RNA-seq alignment of 656 poly(A) libraries (SU2C n=482 in two batches, UW-TAN n=174) to hg38 with STAR v2.7.3a and gene-level quantification with the GenomicAlignments Bioconductor package; batch homogeneity confirmed by multidimensional scaling - STAR is pinned, but GenomicAlignments, Bioconductor and R carry no version, no STAR index/GTF is identified, and no STAR parameters are given

Differential gene expression analysis with edgeR and limma using filterByExpr filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction - no edgeR/limma/R versions, no design matrix, no normalisation method (TMM vs voom) and no significance thresholds stated

Computation of the 31-gene cell cycle progression (CCP), 10-gene androgen receptor activity (ARa) and 10-gene neuroendocrine activity (NEa) scores using GSVA on log2 FPKM RNA-Seq data with 'validated gene panels', standardized across the cohort - the three gene panels are referenced to prior publications rather than listed, GSVA carries no version and no kcdf/method arguments, and no scoring script is released

Immune infiltration deconvolution performed independently per cohort with CIBERSORT v1.04 using the LM22 signature matrix, absolute mode enabled and 100 permutations, followed by per-subgroup mean and median immune-cell frequencies - tool pinned, signature matrix named, mode and permutation count exact; quantile normalisation setting not stated

Clonal architecture and phylogenetic reconstruction with PhyloWGS v1.0-rc2 on multi-sample WGS, inputs prepared with the PhyloWGS parser from high-quality VCF calls, Sequenza segmented copy number and cellularity estimates, DDR-pathway simple somatic mutations prioritized, MCMC with four independent parallel chains - tool pinned and chain count exact, but no burn-in, sample count, thinning or seed, and 'prioritized' is not operationalised

Visualisation of subclonal architecture, clonal frequency dynamics across metastatic sites and evolutionary trajectories with Clonevol v0.1 - tool pinned but no clustering input specification, no plotting arguments and no released script

Selection of the optimal TMB cut-point maximising MSI-High enrichment by binary logistic regression with three-fold cross-validation, yielding 18.61 mut/Mb and defining the TMB-vH (>=18.61) versus TMB-H (10-18.61) classes - no software, no package, no version, no seed and no fold assignment reported; results appear only in Supplementary Fig. 2B-E

Percent genome alteration (PGA) estimation with the homebrew tool 'PGA_Calculator', cited in the Fig. 2 legend as https://github.com/Niel20/PGA_Estimator with Supplementary Document 6 - the URL returns HTTP 404, no version or release tag is given, and no algorithm parameters (segment thresholds, ploidy handling) appear in the main text

CHIMERA-DDR model construction: two-tier nested Random Forest over 51 genomic and transcriptomic features, Tier-1 stratifying TMB-vH / TMB-H / HRRm / DDR-intact and Tier-2 refining into 7 subgroups by tumor-suppressor and pathway status, producing combined probability scores for admixed DDR phenotypes - no Random Forest implementation named (no R randomForest/ranger, no scikit-learn), no version, no hyperparameters (ntree, mtry, node size, class weighting), no seed, no training/holdout split description in the main text, and the code repository https://github.com/Niel20/CHIMERA returns HTTP 404 under an all-rights-reserved by-request licence

CHIMERA-DDR performance evaluation and overfit assessment: semi-independent test-set evaluation and application to the 52-sample multi-site WGS test cohort from 24 patients with 51 regenerated input features, reported as AUCs 0.919-0.999 - the overfitting protection analysis lives in Supplementary Document 2, the AUC computation software is not named, and both the model code and the stated tertiary-analysis input repository (https://github.com/Niel20/CHIMERA_DDR_Validation_Cohort_52_WGS, HTTP 404) are unavailable

Comparative statistics and figure generation across the 11 DDR subgroups: Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for continuous features (TMB, ploidy, PGA, LOH), Fisher's exact tests for categorical features (MSI, Scar), Pearson correlation for expression relationships, with a multi-tier significance annotation scheme - tests are named and thresholds annotated in figure legends, but no software, package, version, multiple-testing scheme for the subgroup grid, or plotting code is provided

headline.static_readiness: 0/23 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI on 4 of 23 computational steps (C11 SigProfilerExtractor v1.1.23 / COSMIC v3.4, C13 STAR v2.7.3a RNA alignment, C16 CIBERSORT v1.04 / LM22, C17 PhyloWGS v1.0-rc2) and NI on the remaining 19. Two independent constraints bind. First, the code axis collapses for every study-specific step: all three GitHub URLs stated in the paper (Niel20/CHIMERA, Niel20/PGA_Estimator, Niel20/CHIMERA_DDR_Validation_Cohort_52_WGS) return HTTP 404, and the Code Availability statement additionally reserves all rights and gates academic use behind a request to the corresponding author, so the CHIMERA-DDR model itself (C21-C22), the homebrew PGA and pyTHiA-CNA tools (C9, C20), the TMB cut-point regression (C19) and all statistics/figure code (C23) score code = 0. Second, no raw-sequence accession exists anywhere in the paper - the Data Availability statement points only to processed-level cBioPortal datahub directories and three GEO RNA-seq series - so every read-level or BAM-level step (C1-C6, C8, C12) scores data = 0 regardless of its exact tool pins. Twelve upstream tools do carry exact prose pins, which is why capture_claim is exact_pins_partial rather than floating, but no lockfile, container image or digest, conda environment or release tag is claimed, so even under stage-2 execution the environment closure could not be established from what the paper declares.
headline.coverage: 23 computational analysis steps assessed from the bioRxiv v2 full-text METHODS ('Study Cohorts', 'DNA Sequence Analysis', 'Variant Calling, Annotation & Tumor Mutation Burden estimation', 'Microsatellite Instability Analysis', 'Pathogenicity Classification', 'Mutational Signature Analysis', 'Copy Number Analysis, LOH & HRD-Scar', 'Subgroup-Specific Consensus Genomic Aberration Analysis', 'Transcriptome Analysis', 'Immune Infiltration Analysis', 'Clonality and Tumor Evolution Analysis') plus the model-construction, cut-point-selection and PGA descriptions carried in RESULTS and figure legends (the CHIMERA-DDR architecture, the 18.61 mut/Mb logistic-regression cut-point and PGA_Calculator have no METHODS subsection of their own). 1 lumped wet-lab step (tissue acquisition, library preparation and WES/WGS/RNA sequencing of the discovery, WGS test and 130-patient clinical validation cohorts) counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope. Coverage = 23/24 (96%) of enumerated steps. Several parameter details are deferred to Supplementary Documents 1, 2, 5 and 6, which were not retrievable at stage 1.

gaps.where: Code availability - all 23 computational steps, binding on C9, C15, C19, C20, C21, C22, C23
gaps.missing: Every code URL stated in the paper is dead. The Code Availability statement reads in full: 'The computer code associated with the CHIMERA-DDR including the trial data and scripts can be accessed at (https://github.com/Niel20/CHIMERA), all rights are reserved to Copyright 2025 Medical College of Wisconsin. For academic usage codes would be made available by request to corresponding author at ndesarkar@mcw.edu.' That URL returns HTTP 404, as do the two other stated repositories (Niel20/PGA_Estimator in the Fig. 2 legend, Niel20/CHIMERA_DDR_Validation_Cohort_52_WGS in Data Availability). Beyond the missing repositories there is no pipeline definition (no Snakemake/Nextflow/WDL), no per-step command line, no Random Forest training script, no statistics or figure code, and the two homebrew tools pyTHiA-CNA and PGA_Calculator exist only as prose descriptions in Supplementary Documents 5 and 6. The all-rights-reserved plus by-request licence means that even if the repository were made public, redistribution and independent re-execution would remain legally constrained.
gaps.how_to_close: Make the CHIMERA-DDR repository public (or deposit it in Zenodo with a DOI and a tagged release), publish pyTHiA-CNA and PGA_Estimator with their algorithms and parameters, add the per-step command lines for the upstream WES/WGS/RNA pipeline, and attach an OSI-approved licence so the code can be executed and redistributed for verification rather than only inspected on request.

gaps.where: Raw sequence data for all read-level steps (C1-C6, C8, C12) and for the clinical validation and WGS test cohorts
gaps.missing: No raw-sequence accession is stated anywhere. The Data Availability statement names only processed-level resources: two cBioPortal datahub directories (public/prad_su2c_2019, public/prad_fhcrc) and three GEO series for UW-TAN bulk RNA-seq (GSE147250, GSE171729, GSE228283). No SRA, dbGaP or EGA identifier is given for the WES or WGS reads, so alignment, duplicate marking, BQSR, germline and somatic calling, TMB, MSI, Sequenza and the pooled-BAM CNVkit consensus analysis cannot be entered at all. The 130-patient clinical validation cohort has no accession and no data-access-committee route; its data appear only as Supplementary Table 7. The 52-sample WGS tertiary files (VCF and *.segment.txt) are directed to a GitHub repository that returns 404.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the WES and WGS reads in dbGaP or EGA with a stated data-access-committee procedure and cite the accession, and re-deposit the 52-sample WGS tertiary analysis files (VCFs and segment tables) in a persistent archive (Zenodo/EGA) with checksums rather than a GitHub repository.

gaps.where: The 51-feature CHIMERA-DDR input matrix and all intermediate derived tables (C19, C21, C22)
gaps.missing: The model's own input is never released. The 51 genomic and transcriptomic features are described narratively but no feature dictionary, no per-sample feature matrix, no class labels for the 466 high-quality discovery samples, no train/test partition and no fold assignment are provided in a machine-readable form. The same applies to the union somatic call set, the Sequenza segment tables, the HRD-Scar component scores and the derived subgroup assignments used by every downstream comparison. Without these, none of C19, C21, C22 or C23 can be entered even by a reader holding all the public cBioPortal and GEO data.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the 51-feature matrix with a feature dictionary (definition, source step, units, transformation), the per-sample subgroup labels, and the exact train/validation/test partitions with the seed used to generate them.

gaps.where: Stochastic steps C11 (SigProfilerExtractor NMF, 100 replicates with resampling), C12 (Picard downsampling to 300x), C17 (PhyloWGS MCMC, 4 chains), C19 (three-fold cross-validated logistic regression), C21 (nested Random Forest training)
gaps.missing: No random seed is reported for any stochastic step. SigProfilerExtractor runs 100 NMF replicates with resampling, Picard DownsampleSam is inherently random, PhyloWGS runs four MCMC chains with unreported burn-in/sample/thinning settings, the TMB cut-point comes from a three-fold cross-validation whose fold assignment is unreported, and the Random Forest has neither seed nor hyperparameters. The headline cut-point of 18.61 mut/Mb and the reported AUC range of 0.919-0.999 are therefore not bit-reproducible.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the seed for every stochastic invocation (NMF, downsampling, MCMC, cross-validation fold generation, Random Forest), the PhyloWGS MCMC settings, and the Random Forest hyperparameters, and publish the driver scripts that set them.

gaps.where: 11 of 23 computational steps (C3, C4, C7, C9, C10, C14, C15, C19, C20, C21, C22, C23) and secondary packages in otherwise-pinned steps
gaps.missing: No version pins for MuTect2, GATK HaplotypeCaller (as used in C3), BEDTools, ANNOVAR, the Sztupinszky HRD-Scar tool, edgeR, limma, GSVA, GenomicAlignments, R itself, or the Random Forest implementation behind CHIMERA-DDR; 'Strelka v2' gives only a major version. The two homebrew tools (pyTHiA-CNA, PGA_Calculator) carry no version or commit at all. Twelve tools are pinned exactly (BWA-MEM v0.7.17.1, Picard v2.24.1, GATK BQSR v4.1.9.0, pyTMB v1.4.0, MSIsensor-pro v1.2.0, SigProfilerExtractor v1.1.23, Sequenza v2.0.0, CNVkit v0.9.12, STAR v2.7.3a, CIBERSORT v1.04, PhyloWGS v1.0-rc2, Clonevol v0.1), which is why the capture claim is exact_pins_partial.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a software table giving an exact version (and git commit where applicable) for every tool and R/Python package used, including R and Bioconductor releases from sessionInfo(), and assign version tags to the two homebrew tools.

gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, container image or digest, conda/mamba environment file, renv.lock or requirements.txt is claimed anywhere in the paper. The stack spans Java (Picard, GATK, CIBERSORT), C/C++ command-line tools (BWA, STAR, MSIsensor-pro, Strelka), Python (pyTMB, SigProfilerExtractor, CNVkit, PhyloWGS, pyTHiA-CNA, PGA_Calculator) and R/Bioconductor (Sequenza, edgeR, limma, GSVA, GenomicAlignments, Clonevol) with no captured dependency closure of any kind. The acknowledgment credits the MCW Research Computing Core with 'the setup of computational terminals, platforms, and environments', which indicates a hand-configured HPC environment that was never serialised.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a container digest or a conda-lock / pixi lockfile (plus renv.lock for the R components) covering the full Java, C/C++, Python and R stacks, and reference it from the Code Availability statement.

gaps.where: Reference genomes, annotation and variant databases (C1, C3, C7, C9, C11, C13)
gaps.missing: Some resources are pinned well - gnomAD v3.1.1, COSMIC v3.4, GENCODE v45, the LM22 signature matrix - but the GRCh38/hg38 reference is given only as a build name with no source (Ensembl vs UCSC vs GDC/1000G analysis set), no FASTA checksum and no decoy/alt-contig policy, which materially changes alignment and signature results; the 1000 Genomes and ESP6500 germline filters carry no release; the BQSR known-sites resources are unnamed; the ANNOVAR annotation databases have no build or download date; and the nine clinical databases used for cross-validation (cBioPortal, ExAC, Kaviar, ClinGen, ClinVar, ClinVitae, CIViC, OncoKB, UniProt) are continuously updated resources cited with no release or access date, so the pathogenicity calls at the base of every DDR subgroup definition cannot be regenerated.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin the exact reference FASTA (source, build, checksum, alt/decoy policy), the BQSR known-sites files, the ANNOVAR database builds, the WES capture BED, and a dated snapshot or release identifier for each of the nine clinical annotation databases; ideally deposit the frozen annotation snapshot used for curation.

gaps.where: All three stated GitHub repositories and the cBioPortal datahub directories
gaps.missing: Three of the four repository-hosted artifacts in the availability statements are already dead at the time of assessment: https://github.com/Niel20/CHIMERA (404), https://github.com/Niel20/PGA_Estimator (404) and https://github.com/Niel20/CHIMERA_DDR_Validation_Cohort_52_WGS (404). The two live cBioPortal datahub links point at the master branch of a continuously updated repository rather than a tagged release or DOI, so the study-relevant snapshot of prad_su2c_2019 and prad_fhcrc cannot be recovered as it stood. Not one of the code or study-specific data artifacts carries a persistent identifier.
gaps.how_to_close: Archive the code and the WGS tertiary analysis files in Zenodo (or Software Heritage) with DOIs and tagged releases, and cite the cBioPortal datahub artifacts by commit hash or by the corresponding cBioPortal study release rather than by master-branch URL.

gaps.where: Cohort definition and quality-control filtering (C1 upstream; Study Cohorts section)
gaps.missing: The sample-count chain is internally inconsistent and unauditable. The Abstract and Results state 672 WES samples comprising 228 UW-TAN plus 444 SU2C, yielding '482 high-quality exomes after rigorous filtering'; the Methods Study Cohorts section states the same 672 total as 270 UW-TAN plus 444 SU2C (which sums to 714, not 672) yielding '466 high-quality samples'. Neither the 482 nor the 466 figure is reconciled, the 'rigorous filtering' and 'quality control filtering to remove low-coverage sequence data' criteria are given no numeric thresholds, and the retained-sample list lives only in Supplementary Table 1. Every downstream percentage in the paper (9.1% TMB-High, 3.9% TMB-vH, 1.2% TMB-H HRRm, 2.3% concurrent, 1.5% MMR bi-allelic) depends on a denominator that cannot be reconstructed.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact QC thresholds (mean target coverage, contamination, tumor purity floor, duplicate rate), reconcile the 228/270 and 482/466 discrepancies, and publish the machine-readable pass/fail sample manifest with per-sample QC metrics.
